usage: Minecraft Java 1.21.1; master engineering handbook is mandatory for redstone/automation requests. Glossary is supplementary; NOT functional testing.

items.name: Redstone Dust
items.purpose: Carries powered signal; power level 0-15 and attenuation
rules: Signal 0..15, attenuates along dust; repeater refreshes 15.
Connections north/east/south/west none/side/up and power are distinct states.
Vanilla normalization cannot fill missing wire gaps.
Analog 1..15 values are meaningful for comparator and threshold logic; dust glow fading is not just decorative.
A powered opaque block does not automatically become a dust segment; support, conduction and direction matter.
Java 1.21.1 predates the optional 1.21.2 redstone experiments; do not assume their update-order behavior.

items.name: Repeater
items.purpose: Directional one-way signal refresh and delay
rules: Java 1.21.1 minecraft:repeater facing property points to its REAR/INPUT side, NOT output; output is OPPOSITE.
Flow from WEST at x-1 to EAST at x+1 requires repeater[facing=west], with rear/input west and output east.
Flow NORTH to SOUTH (+Z) requires repeater[facing=north]. Delay=1..4 REDSTONE ticks =2..8 game ticks.
Side-locking can preserve state and must not be mistakenly reversed in a complex circuit. Independent support block required.
A short pulse (e.g., 1 redstone tick) may widen to the configured 4-redstone-tick delay; a repeater cannot substitute for a multi-second hold-open timer.
RIGHT unit conversion: 1 redstone tick=2 game ticks, 0.1s at nominal 20 TPS.

items.name: Comparator
items.purpose: Compare, subtract and container signal reading
rules: Java 1.21.1 minecraft:comparator facing points to REAR/INPUT, not output; front output is opposite.
Flow WEST input to EAST output requires comparator[facing=west,mode=compare,powered=false].
Compare rear if >= side else 0; subtract max(0,rear-side); may read tile/block-entity inventories.
Side analog readings, mode, substrate and output signal must remain correct on rotation.
Compare mode outputs rear input if rear >= maximum side input, otherwise 0. Subtract outputs max(0,rear-maximum side).
Unlike a repeater, the comparator does not automatically renew any nonzero input to 15.

items.name: Observer
items.purpose: Detect adjacent block changes and produce brief pulse
rules: Observed side opposite output face; facing/output orientation is critical.
Detects eligible adjacent block-state changes; very short Java pulse.
Observer clocks can create expensive feedback; include disabling control.

items.name: Piston
items.purpose: Extend head and push limited attached line of blocks
rules: Facing extension, max 12 movable blocks, clearance/immovable check.
Java quasi-connectivity: power of block above can trigger after neighbor update.
Short pulses, QC and update order affect behavior.
Java QC can cause activation via powered space above piston, but a neighbor update may still be required.
Do not assume Bedrock 'one tick extend / zero tick retract' descriptions describe Java piston event execution.

items.name: Sticky Piston
rules: Pushes up to 12, normally pulls one movable block on retraction.
Short pulse may drop block, Java QC/update order matter.
Nonmovable blocks halt extension; check full adhesive mass.

items.name: Hopper
items.purpose: Transfers and collects item entities/inventory items
rules: Facing selects outgoing destination; powered hopper LOCKS transfers.
Throughput/cooldown matter for sorter/clocks; needs real inventory NBT.
A hopper underneath/pointing into an inventory behaves differently.
Vanilla enabled hopper transfer baseline one item per 8 game ticks (0.4s) at full TPS; power locks hopper.
Zero real items means a hopper clock is not configured; avoid claiming timer works from geometry only.

items.name: Dropper
items.purpose: Ejects or transfers an item on pulse
rules: facing points where output goes
Does not use special item behavior
Java QC can trigger through the space above; verify neighbor update.
Needs actual inventory; powered changes do not magically create items.

items.name: Dispenser
items.purpose: Uses or dispenses item on pulse
rules: facing matters
Behavior depends on item
Power edge required to activate
Java QC can trigger through power to the space above; block update may be required.
Requires real inventory to use water bucket or bone meal; BuildAI block-only blueprints do not preload.

items.name: Redstone Torch
rules: Wall variant has facing property
Rapid repeated activation can burn out

items.name: Lever
rules: face=floor|wall|ceiling
facing changes placement
powered boolean determines output

items.name: Stone Button
rules: powered is transient
wall or floor/ceiling mounting
Java stone/polished blackstone press lasts 20 game ticks (10 redstone ticks) at normal TPS; wooden button lasts 30 game ticks (15 redstone ticks).

items.name: Weighted Pressure Plate
rules: Must have floor support
Threshold differs from light plate

items.name: Daylight Detector
rules: Power depends on sky light
inverted flag changes behavior

items.name: Target Block
items.purpose: Power pulse when struck by projectile
rules: Output depends on hit accuracy
Requires valid interaction from projectile

items.name: Redstone Lamp
rules: Lit flag changes with nearby signal
Light level affects nearby environment

items.name: Sculk Sensor
rules: Wool can occlude vibration paths
Signal strength depends on vibration event

items.name: Powered Rail
rules: Use AS NEEDED, not at every track cell; an unpowered powered rail BRAKES.
Rough level occupied passenger cart benchmark one powered rail per ~38 track blocks; uphill and heavy minecarts require denser boosts.
One nearby redstone source can power a rail plus up to 8 contiguous rails either direction. Do not put redstone blocks under every powered rail.
Rail shape and correct power matter; no perpetual propulsion without actual power.

items.name: Detector Rail
rules: Shape must connect
Triggers when cart passes

items.name: Activator Rail
rules: Activator rails interact with certain cart contents/passengers; they are NOT propulsion rails.
Use only where cart activation/ejection is requested, with controlled powered status.

items.name: Iron Door
rules: Lower and upper halves align
facing and hinge must match
Needs external power

items.name: Iron Trapdoor

items.name: Note Block

rules: instrument depends on block underneath
note state 0-24
Blocks overhead can suppress sound

items.name: Tripwire Hook
rules: Connected hooks with supported tripwire span
Powered and attached states

items.name: Crafter
rules: New power pulse crafts one recipe, constant power does not continually craft.
Comparator strength 0..9 counts occupied OR disabled slots, NOT ingredient quantities.
Requires actual recipe items, disabled slots/block entity beyond basic schematic blockstates.
Output via front/facing; Java quasi-connectivity does NOT apply.
No Java QC, unlike droppers and dispensers.

items.name: Copper Bulb
rules: Rising-edge power toggles persistent lit state; distinct from lamp.
Oxidation changes emitted LIGHT (15/12/8/4), NOT TIMING. Wax to preserve light.
Comparator reads lit status 15/on or 0/off; bulb is not ordinary conductor.
The rising-edge toggling function may replace unnecessarily large T-flip-flop memories if that meets the original player's requirements.

rules: May unintentionally quasi-power pistons
Not a substitute for a pulse

Avoid rapid loops

Needs support

Needs support

items.name: Trapped Chest
items.purpose: Power when a player opens it
rules: Distinct from minecraft:chest; a trapped chest emits redstone signal when a player opens it (one per player up to strength 15). Ordinary chest never emits this opening signal.
Trapped chest retains normal chest storage functionality; its comparator inventory-fullness output is separate from the opening-event signal.
Do not replace ordinary storage chests with trapped chests unless explicitly requested or the opener-trigger signal is required.
Opening-power is NOT equivalent to comparator-fullness power. Verify which source the player asked for.

Occupied level cart typical booster about one powered rail per 38 rails; adjust for speed and terrain.

items.placement: ENTITY, not a placeable block state. Requires entity spawn/serialization, which a normal block-only schematic does not provide.

items.name: Water Source
items.purpose: World-placed irrigation, flushing, canals, water flows
rules: minecraft:water source is a block, not minecraft:water_bucket which is an item.
Creative source placement costs nothing; NEVER block a Creative generation for water buckets.
Survival requires exactly TWO water_bucket items TOTAL per build as renewable starter water, even for many placed source cells.
Charge once during final fluid normalization, return both empty buckets to marked supply chests, then place all water sources.
Finish containment, crop channels and redstone before fluid placement. An actual fluid-handling dispenser needs its own real inventory buckets.

items.name: Lava Source
items.purpose: World-placed decorative/functional lava channel or source
rules: minecraft:lava is a block, lava_bucket is an item.
Creative placement is free; Survival costs ONE lava_bucket item for EACH lava source cell.
Charge per source during final fluid normalization and return each empty bucket to marked supply chest.
Containment and fire/stone reaction safety are mandatory; never apply the renewable-water two-bucket rule to lava.
Actual dispensing of lava during game operation needs separate block-entity bucket inventory setup.
Ordinary chest is storage only; no redstone power is emitted by opening or closing it.
Comparator pointing into a regular chest outputs analog strength reflecting inventory fullness (0..15), not the chest lid state.
Default for generic storage, normal/simple/plain/regular chest requests. Do not substitute trapped_chest merely because redstone exists nearby.

designContract: redstone_plan.circuits with name,input,signalPath,output,timing,reset,test. Design real geometry and correct facing/mode.
versionSpecificCorrections: Repeater and comparator FACING denotes REAR/INPUT, not output, in Java 1.21.1; output lies opposite.
Powered rails are sparse boosters, not a universal replacement for normal rails; power sources need not appear below each rail.
Creative fluid source blocks cost no buckets; Survival charges two water buckets total per build, one lava bucket per lava source, and returns empties.
